abstract: Interpretability has gained an immense amount of popularity over the past decade, mostly riding the wake of neural networks’ impact on the field of machine learning. The growth in success and application of neural networks, as well as other blackbox machine learning approaches, in everyday life has led to a revitalized interest in understanding the blackbox models making those decisions. In this survey, we give a holistic coverage of the current state of the interpretability literature, focusing on a detailed coverage only for machine learning tasks and feature interaction methods like SHAP explanations, functional ANOVA, and the generalized additive model. We achieve this by first mapping out the many different subareas and paradigms under the larger umbrella of the Interpretability or XAI literature. We next isolate the scope of this survey and provide a detailed account of historical developments leading to the modern convergence of interpretability through feature interactions and interpretability through additive models. Finally, we conclude with a discussion of specific domains of application and with future directions for interpretability.
title: A Detailed Survey of Machine Learning Interpretability through Feature Interactions and Additive Models
